parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **scarcity**?
choices: The human effort, physical and mental, used in the production of goods and services
Natural resources used in production, such as minerals, soil, forests and water
The situation where resources are limited/finite while wants are unlimited, so choices must be made
Man-made resources used to produce other goods and services, such as machinery or buildings

rows.answer:

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **production possibility curve (PPC)**?
choices: A curve showing the maximum combinations of two goods/services that can be produced when all resources are fully and efficiently used
The amount of one good that must be given up to produce more of the other good when moving along the curve
A combination of goods outside the curve which cannot be produced with the current resources and technology
Producing at a point on the PPC so it is not possible to produce more of one good without producing less of the other

rows.answer: A curve showing the maximum combinations of two goods/services that can be produced when all resources are fully and efficiently used.
rows.notes: Award 1 mark for a precise definition. Do not award the mark for an example alone.

parts.text: What is meant by the term **production possibility curve (PPC)**?

rows.answer: A curve showing the maximum combinations of two goods/services (1) that can be produced when all resources are fully and efficiently used (1).
rows.notes: Award 1 mark for the key idea of the definition and 1 mark for a valid developing point, which may be a relevant example such as the one shown. An example given without the key idea gains a maximum of 1 mark.

parts.text: Define the term **productive efficiency (on a PPC)**.

rows.answer: Producing at a point on the PPC so it is not possible to produce more of one good without producing less of the other.
rows.notes: Award 1 mark for a precise definition. Do not award the mark for an example alone.

parts.text: What is meant by the term **productive efficiency (on a PPC)**?

rows.answer: Producing at a point on the PPC (1) so it is not possible to produce more of one good without producing less of the other (1).
rows.notes: Award 1 mark for the key idea of the definition and 1 mark for a valid developing point, which may be a relevant example such as the one shown. An example given without the key idea gains a maximum of 1 mark.

parts.text: Define the term **an unattainable point on a PPC**.

rows.answer: A combination of goods outside the curve which cannot be produced with the current resources and technology.
rows.notes: Award 1 mark for a precise definition. Do not award the mark for an example alone.

parts.text: What is meant by the term **an unattainable point on a PPC**?

parts.text: Define the term **economic growth (shown on a PPC)**.

rows.answer: An outward shift of the PPC showing an increase in the productive capacity of the economy.

parts.text: Define the term **unemployment of resources (on a PPC)**.

parts.text: Define the term **opportunity cost (on a PPC)**.

rows.answer: The amount of one good that must be given up to produce more of the other good when moving along the curve.

Explain why this decision may still be consistent with the assumption that workers maximise their rewards.

rows.answer:
Award 1 mark for identifying a relevant point, 1 mark for developing it and 1 mark for applying it to the context.

Example:
- Rewards include non-financial benefits (1); staying close to home saves travel time and costs (1), so Nia's total reward from the current job may be greater than the higher wage at Riverstone Ltd (1)
rows.notes: Accept any other valid explanation. Answers with no reference to the context cannot gain the third mark.

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **demand**?
choices: A good for which demand rises when incomes rise
A good for which demand falls when incomes rise, as consumers switch to better alternatives
A fall in quantity demanded caused by a rise in the price of the product itself (movement up the demand curve)
The amount of a product that buyers want and can afford to purchase at each price over a period of time

rows.answer:
Correct option: **D** (The amount of a product that buyers want and can afford to purchase at each price over a period of time)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of a normal good
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of an inferior good
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of a contraction in demand

Award 1 mark for identifying a relevant point, 1 mark for developing it and 1 mark for applying it to the context.

- Demand for the substitute would rise (1) because consumers switch away from the more expensive beef (1), so at each price more of the substitute is bought after the 12% rise (1)

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **supply**?
choices: A rise in quantity supplied caused by a rise in the price of the product (movement up the supply curve)
A fall in quantity supplied caused by a fall in the price of the product (movement down the supply curve)
The amount of a product that firms are prepared to offer for sale at each price over a period of time
A tax on spending/goods and services which raises firms' costs and reduces supply

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (The amount of a product that firms are prepared to offer for sale at each price over a period of time)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of an extension in supply
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of a contraction in supply
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of an indirect tax

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **an extension in supply**?
choices: A fall in quantity supplied caused by a fall in the price of the product (movement down the supply curve)
The amount of a product that firms are prepared to offer for sale at each price over a period of time
A tax on spending/goods and services which raises firms' costs and reduces supply
A rise in quantity supplied caused by a rise in the price of the product (movement up the supply curve)

rows.answer:
Correct option: **D** (A rise in quantity supplied caused by a rise in the price of the product (movement up the supply curve))
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of a contraction in supply
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of supply
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of an indirect tax

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **a contraction in supply**?
choices: A fall in quantity supplied caused by a fall in the price of the product (movement down the supply curve)
The payments a firm makes for the factors of production it uses such as wages, rent and raw materials
A rise in quantity supplied caused by a rise in the price of the product (movement up the supply curve)
A payment from the government to producers which lowers costs and increases supply

rows.answer:
Correct option: **A** (A fall in quantity supplied caused by a fall in the price of the product (movement down the supply curve))
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of costs of production
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of an extension in supply
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of a subsidy

higher prices make it more profitable to produce more
consumers buy more at higher prices

intro:
The price of olive oil has risen by 54% in two years. Poor harvests in major producing countries have reduced supply, while demand from younger consumers has continued to grow.

Two of the largest producing countries reported harvests 15% below normal because of extreme weather and plant disease. Stocks held by traders have fallen to their lowest level for 17 years.

At the same time, consumption in younger consumers has risen by about 4% a year. Farmers in several countries have started planting new trees, but these take three to five years to produce a full crop. Some food manufacturers have reduced the size of their products rather than raise prices.

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **price elasticity of demand (PED)**?
choices: When quantity demanded does not change at all whatever happens to price (PED = 0)
A measure of how strongly the amount bought reacts when the price of the product changes
When a change in price leads to a proportionately smaller change in quantity demanded (PED less than 1, ignoring the sign)
The money a firm receives from selling its output calculated as price multiplied by quantity sold

rows.answer:
Correct option: **B** (A measure of how strongly the amount bought reacts when the price of the product changes)
A: incorrect, that is the meaning of perfectly inelastic demand
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of price inelastic demand
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of total revenue

parts.text:
Sunvale plc sells branded trainers in Doha. It estimates that the PED for its product is -1.8.

Explain whether Sunvale plc should increase or decrease its price to increase total revenue.

rows.answer:
Award 1 mark for identifying a relevant point, 1 mark for developing it and 1 mark for applying it to the context.

Example:
- Sunvale plc should decrease its price (1) because demand is price elastic, as PED of -1.8 is greater than 1 ignoring the sign (1), so quantity demanded rises by a larger percentage than the price falls, raising total revenue (1)
rows.notes: Accept any other valid explanation. Answers with no reference to the context cannot gain the third mark.

Redwood & Co is the only bus operator in Dublin. It plans to raise fares by 15%. Many passengers rely on buses to get to work, but some routes are also served by trains and a new bicycle-hire scheme.

Redwood & Co carries about 60,000 passengers a day. The single fare is €2.40. A survey found that 60% of passengers use the bus to get to work and 17% are students or pensioners.

Train services cover only 6 of the city's 35 bus routes. The bicycle-hire scheme has 1133 bikes and charges €1 for 30 minutes. When Redwood & Co last raised fares, by 5% three years ago, passenger numbers fell by about 2%.

intro:
The government of Halvoria wants to raise revenue and reduce consumption of sugary drinks. It is considering a tax that would raise the price by 28%. Studies suggest the PED for sugary drinks is about -0.3.

Consumers in Halvoria spend H€5bn a year on sugary drinks. The government estimates that illnesses linked to sugary drinks cost the health service H€1bn a year.

A neighbouring country introduced a similar tax three years ago. Consumption there fell by about 10% in the first year, and tax revenue was higher than expected. However, some consumers began buying sugary drinks across the border where prices are lower, and low-income households spend a larger share of their income on sugary drinks.

intro:

Kestrel & Co carries about 29,000 passengers a day. The single fare is NZ\$1.80. A survey found that 71% of passengers use the bus to get to work and 20% are students or pensioners.

figures.text:
The government of Ostrelia wants to raise revenue and reduce consumption of cigarettes. It is considering a tax that would raise the price by 26%. Studies suggest the PED for cigarettes is about -0.6.

Consumers in Ostrelia spend O£5bn a year on cigarettes. The government estimates that illnesses linked to cigarettes cost the health service O£3bn a year.

A neighbouring country introduced a similar tax three years ago. Consumption there fell by about 6% in the first year, and tax revenue was higher than expected. parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **price elasticity of supply (PES)**?
choices: The responsiveness of quantity supplied to a change in price
When a change in price causes a proportionately smaller change in quantity supplied (PES less than 1)
When quantity supplied cannot change whatever the price (PES = 0)
When a firm is producing less than the maximum it could with its existing resources

rows.answer:
Correct option: **A** (The responsiveness of quantity supplied to a change in price)
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of price inelastic supply
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of perfectly inelastic supply
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of spare capacity

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **price elastic supply**?

Award 1 mark for a relevant point and 1 mark for a linked development, for example:

- land for building is scarce (1) so builders cannot easily increase supply (1)

intro:
House prices in Penang have risen by 12% in a year. Builders say a shortage of land, a lack of skilled workers and slow planning permission mean they cannot build new homes quickly.

The average house price in Penang is now RM287,000, about 9 times average earnings. Builders completed 3,000 homes last year, while the number of households grew by 5,000.

Planning permission takes on average 24 months. The construction industry says it has 7,000 unfilled vacancies for bricklayers, electricians and plumbers. The city council has said it will release land it owns for building, but this will take several years.

intro:
In Ostrelia, most goods and services are provided by private firms. The government provides healthcare, education, roads and defence, financed by taxes that take about 32% of national income.

Public spending in Ostrelia is O£48bn a year. Healthcare and education take 45% of this. The state also owns the railway, which made a loss of O£875 million last year.

A business group says lower taxes would encourage investment and that private firms could run some services more efficiently. However, a survey found 70% of people want free healthcare to continue, and in areas where private schools charge fees, attendance by children from low-income families is low.

intro:
In Eskaria, most goods and services are provided by private firms. The government provides healthcare, education, roads and defence, financed by taxes that take about 45% of national income.

Public spending in Eskaria is E\$48bn a year. Healthcare and education take 49% of this. The state also owns the railway, which made a loss of E\$704 million last year.

A business group says lower taxes would encourage investment and that private firms could run some services more efficiently. However, a survey found 75% of people want free healthcare to continue, and in areas where private schools charge fees, attendance by children from low-income families is low.

A survey found 72% of residents feel unsafe walking at night. Police figures show street crime rose by 18% last year. Installing lights would cost about Z£35 million, plus Z£3 million a year to run.

Once a street light is installed, everyone who walks along the street benefits, whether or not they have paid. Some shopkeepers say they would contribute, but most residents say they would not pay voluntarily. The government already faces a budget deficit.

parts.text: An indirect tax on a product will shift
choices: the supply curve to the left
the demand curve to the left
the supply curve to the right
the demand curve to the right

rows.answer:
Correct option: **A** (the supply curve to the left)
B: incorrect
C: incorrect
D: incorrect

parts.text: A subsidy to producers is likely to result in
choices: a higher price and higher quantity
a higher price and lower quantity
a lower price and a higher quantity
no change in price

rows.answer:
Correct option: **C** (a lower price and a higher quantity)
A: incorrect
B: incorrect
D: incorrect

parts.text: Define the term **indirect tax**.

rows.answer: A tax on spending on goods and services collected from firms, which raises costs and reduces supply.
rows.notes: Award 1 mark for a precise definition. Do not award the mark for an example alone.

parts.text: What is meant by the term **indirect tax**?

rows.answer: A tax on spending on goods and services (1) collected from firms, which raises costs and reduces supply (1).
rows.notes: Award 1 mark for the key idea of the definition and 1 mark for a valid developing point, which may be a relevant example such as the one shown. An example given without the key idea gains a maximum of 1 mark.

parts.text: Define the term **subsidy**.

rows.answer: A payment by the government to producers to reduce their costs and increase supply.
rows.notes: Award 1 mark for a precise definition. Do not award the mark for an example alone.

parts.text: What is meant by the term **subsidy**?

rows.answer: A payment by the government to producers (1) to reduce their costs and increase supply (1).
rows.notes: Award 1 mark for the key idea of the definition and 1 mark for a valid developing point, which may be a relevant example such as the one shown. An example given without the key idea gains a maximum of 1 mark.

parts.text: Define the term **regulation**.

rows.answer: Rules or laws set by the government to control the behaviour of firms or consumers.

intro:
The government of Eskaria wants more people to use electric cars. It is considering either a subsidy of E\$3,000 for each electric car sold, or a tax on petrol and diesel cars.

About 2% of new cars sold in Eskaria last year were electric. Electric cars cost on average E\$7,000 more than a similar petrol car. There are only 1404 public charging points in the country.

The subsidy would cost the government an estimated E\$312 million a year. A tax on petrol and diesel cars would raise revenue, but car dealers say it would hit rural drivers who have few alternatives. A neighbouring country that introduced a subsidy saw electric car sales rise to 19% of new cars within four years.

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **externality**?
choices: A cost or benefit to a third party not involved in the production or consumption of a good
The cost of an activity paid by third parties rather than the producer or consumer
The total cost to society of an activity equal to private cost plus external cost
The cost of an activity paid by the individual or firm carrying it out

rows.answer:
Correct option: **A** (A cost or benefit to a third party not involved in the production or consumption of a good)
B: incorrect, that is the meaning of external cost
C: incorrect, that is the meaning of social cost
D: incorrect, that is the meaning of private cost

parts.text: Which one of the following best describes **negative externality**?
choices: The cost of an activity paid by the individual or firm carrying it out
A cost to third parties from the production or consumption of a good, such as pollution
The total benefit to society of an activity equal to private benefit plus external benefit
The total cost to society of an activity equal to private cost plus external cost

rows.answer:

intro:
The government of Zentara banned single-use plastic bags five years ago. Beaches and rivers are cleaner, but inspectors say some shops still give out bags illegally, and enforcement is costly.

Before the ban, an estimated 3 billion plastic bags were used each year in Zentara. A survey of beaches found 68% less plastic waste than in the year before the ban. The ban is enforced by about 120 inspectors, at a cost of Z£7 million a year.

Shops caught giving out bags can be fined up to Z£1929. Inspectors found bags being given out in 10% of market stalls they visited last year. Some shops have switched to paper bags, which cost more to produce.

intro:

figures.text:
The government of Valdoria banned single-use plastic bags five years ago. Beaches and rivers are cleaner, but inspectors say some shops still give out bags illegally, and enforcement is costly.

Before the ban, an estimated 3 billion plastic bags were used each year in Valdoria. A survey of beaches found 67% less plastic waste than in the year before the ban. The ban is enforced by about 123 inspectors, at a cost of V\$17 million a year.

Shops caught giving out bags can be fined up to V\$618. Inspectors found bags being given out in 17% of market stalls they visited last year. Some shops have switched to paper bags, which cost more to produce.

intro:

Shopkeepers fear fewer customers. Low-income drivers own a larger share of older cars, and an electric car costs about V\$33,000 even with the grant.

intro:
